## Summary

Sentry issue `NUKE-DEV-G9` is a real bug in `bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent` at `main.go:241`, filed automatically by the sentry-fix-agent from the High/High real bug deep verdict — that verdict is the approval gate, so this spec is approved rather than drafted.

## Problem

exitErrorForStatus (main.go:241) raises a generic error without the phase's Result.Message, so every failed phase across planning/execution/ai_review collapses into one untriageable Sentry issue; fail-closed ai_review branches (steps_ai_review.go:294 concerns / :171 PR-no-longer-draft) turn transient review errors and human-takeover races into failed tasks.

## Recommended Fix

Pass result.Message into exitErrorForStatus and add a per-phase Sentry fingerprint so failures are self-describing and separable; do not suppress the escalation. Follow-up: retry/classify transient ai_review failures before failing closed.

1	// Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Borbe All rights reserved.
2	// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style
3	// license that can be found in the LICENSE file.
4	
5	// Command github-dark-factory-agent is the canonical AI-heavy agent: one Claude
6	// invocation per phase, all logic in the prompt + allowed tools.
7	//
8	// This binary is the Kafka entry point — spawned as a K8s Job by
9	// task/executor with TASK_CONTENT + TASK_ID + PHASE + KAFKA_BROKERS env.
10	// For local CLI mode (file-based), see cmd/run-task/main.go.
11	//
12	// Reference implementation for AI-heavy agents using the agent framework
13	// (lib.NewAgent + claude.NewAgentStep). Other agents (trade-analysis,
14	// pr-reviewer) follow the same shape — copy this main.go and swap
15	// prompts/tools.
16	package main
17	
18	import (
19		"context"
20		"os"
21		"time"
22	
23		agentlib "github.com/bborbe/agent"
24		claudelib "github.com/bborbe/agent/claude"
25		delivery "github.com/bborbe/agent/delivery"
26		"github.com/bborbe/agent/envparse"
27		libmetrics "github.com/bborbe/agent/metrics"
28		"github.com/bborbe/cqrs/base"
29		"github.com/bborbe/errors"
30		libkafka "github.com/bborbe/kafka"
31		githubapp "github.com/bborbe/maintainer/githubapp"
32		libsentry "github.com/bborbe/sentry"
33		"github.com/bborbe/service"
34		libtime "github.com/bborbe/time"
35		"github.com/bborbe/vault-cli/pkg/domain"
36		"github.com/golang/glog"
37		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"
38		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/push"
39	
40		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/factory"
41		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/githubauth"
42	)
43	
44	// agentName is the identity string used for Prometheus metric grouping and logging.
45	const agentName = "github-dark-factory-agent"
46	
47	func main() {
48		app := &application{}
49		os.Exit(service.Main(context.Background(), app, &app.SentryDSN, &app.SentryProxy))
50	}
51	
52	type application struct {
53		SentryDSN   string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-dsn"   env:"SENTRY_DSN"   usage:"SentryDSN"    display:"length"`
54		SentryProxy string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-proxy" env:"SENTRY_PROXY" usage:"Sentry Proxy" display:"length"`
55	
56		// Claude Code CLI configuration
57		ClaudeConfigDir claudelib.ClaudeConfigDir `required:"false" arg:"claude-config-dir" env:"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" usage:"Claude Code config directory"`
58	
59		// Agent directory (contains .claude/ with CLAUDE.md and commands)
60		AgentDir claudelib.AgentDir `required:"false" arg:"agent-dir" env:"AGENT_DIR" usage:"Agent directory with .claude/ config" default:"agent"`
61	
62		// Allowed tools (comma-separated)
63		AllowedToolsRaw string `required:"false" arg:"allowed-tools" env:"ALLOWED_TOOLS" usage:"Comma-separated list of allowed tools"`
64	
65		// Task content from agent pipeline
66		TaskContent string `required:"true" arg:"task-content" env:"TASK_CONTENT" usage:"Raw task markdown from vault"`
67	
68		// Environment context passed to prompt (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs)
69		EnvContextRaw string `required:"false" arg:"env-context" env:"ENV_CONTEXT" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for prompt context"`
70	
71		// Environment variables passed to Claude CLI process (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs).
72		// Use this for ad-hoc / less-common env vars. The three load-bearing Anthropic provider
73		// vars below have dedicated arg slots so they don't have to be packed into this string.
74		ClaudeEnvRaw string `required:"false" arg:"claude-env" env:"CLAUDE_ENV" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for Claude CLI environment"`
75	
76		// Anthropic-compatible provider routing. Setting AnthropicBaseURL + AnthropicAuthToken
77		// routes the claude CLI to an alt-provider (e.g. MiniMax via https://api.minimax.io/anthropic).
78		// AnthropicModel drives both the `--model` CLI flag and the ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var seen by
79		// the claude subprocess. Non-empty values override the same keys in ClaudeEnvRaw.
80		AnthropicBaseURL   string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-base-url"   env:"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"   usage:"Anthropic-compatible API base URL"`
81		AnthropicAuthToken string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-auth-token" env:"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" usage:"Bearer token for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"                                  display:"length"`
82		AnthropicModel     claudelib.ClaudeModel `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-model"      env:"ANTHROPIC_MODEL"      usage:"Model name; also exposed to the claude subprocess as ANTHROPIC_MODEL"                  default:"sonnet"`
83	
84		// Branch for Kafka result delivery
85		Branch base.Branch `required:"false" arg:"branch" env:"BRANCH" usage:"branch"`
86	
87		// TopicPrefix is an explicit Kafka topic prefix, independent of Branch.
88		TopicPrefix base.TopicPrefix `required:"false" arg:"topic-prefix" env:"TOPIC_PREFIX" usage:"Explicit Kafka topic prefix; empty means unprefixed topics"`
89	
90		// Phase to run (framework requires explicit phase)
91		Phase domain.TaskPhase `required:"false" arg:"phase" env:"PHASE" usage:"Agent phase: planning | execution | ai_review" default:"execution"`
92	
93		// GitHub token for authenticated clones + REST API calls (planning phase).
94		// Used as the raw fallback credential when GitHub App creds are absent
95		// (local cmd/run-task path where the operator exports `gh auth token`).
96		GhToken string `required:"false" arg:"gh-token" env:"GH_TOKEN" usage:"GitHub token for clone + PR inspection (raw fallback when App creds unset)" display:"length"`
97	
98		// GitHub App authentication. When APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file
99		// or inline) are all set, the pod mints a short-lived installation access
100		// token at startup and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess as GH_TOKEN.
101		// The cluster pod sets these (GH_TOKEN is empty there); locally they are
102		// absent and the agent falls back to the raw GhToken above.
103		AppID          int64  `required:"false" arg:"app-id"          env:"APP_ID"          usage:"GitHub App ID (numeric); enables App auth when set with INSTALLATION_ID + PEM"`
104		InstallationID int64  `required:"false" arg:"installation-id" env:"INSTALLATION_ID" usage:"GitHub App Installation ID (numeric)"`
105		PEMKeyFile     string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key-file"    env:"PEM_KEY_FILE"    usage:"Path to the GitHub App private key (PEM file mounted from k8s Secret)"`
106		PEMKey         string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key"         env:"PEM_KEY"         usage:"GitHub App private key (PEM) as env var content; mutually exclusive with PEM_KEY_FILE" display:"length"`
107	
108		// Workdir paths for bare-clone cache and per-task worktrees.
109		ReposPath string `required:"false" arg:"repos-path" env:"REPOS_PATH" usage:"Root path for bare-clone cache"   default:"/repos"`
110		WorkPath  string `required:"false" arg:"work-path"  env:"WORK_PATH"  usage:"Root path for per-task worktrees" default:"/work"`
111	
112		// Kafka delivery (optional — only active when TASK_ID is set)
113		KafkaBrokers libkafka.Brokers        `required:"false" arg:"kafka-brokers" env:"KAFKA_BROKERS" usage:"Comma separated list of Kafka brokers"`
114		TaskID       agentlib.TaskIdentifier `required:"false" arg:"task-id"       env:"TASK_ID"       usage:"Agent task identifier for publishing results back to task controller"`
115	
116		PushgatewayURL string `required:"false" arg:"pushgateway-url" env:"PUSHGATEWAY_URL" usage:"Prometheus PushGateway URL"          default:"http://pushgateway:9090"`
117		TaskType       string `required:"false" arg:"task-type"       env:"TASK_TYPE"       usage:"Task type label for metric grouping" default:"unknown"`
118	}
119	
120	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
121		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
122		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())
123		pusher := push.New(a.PushgatewayURL, libmetrics.BuildJobMetricsName(agentName)).
124			Grouping("agent", agentName).
125			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
126			Collector(registry)
127		defer func() {
128			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
129				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)
130				return
131			}
132			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
133		}()
134		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
135	
136		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
137	
138		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
139		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
140		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
141		if err != nil {
142			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
143			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
144			return err
145		}
146	
147		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
148		if a.TaskID != "" {
149			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
150				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
151				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
152				return errors.Errorf(ctx, "KAFKA_BROKERS must be set when TASK_ID is set")
153			}
154			syncProducer, err := factory.CreateSyncProducer(ctx, a.KafkaBrokers)
155			if err != nil {
156				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
157				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
158				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
159			}
160			defer func() {
161				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
162					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
163				}
164			}()
165			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
166				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
167				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
168			)
169		}
170	
171		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
172	
173		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
174		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
175		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
176		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
177			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
178			a.AgentDir,
179			a.AnthropicModel,
180			resolvedToken,
181			claudeEnv,
182			repoManager,
183			githubClient,
184			claudeProber,
185			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
186			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
187			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
188			a.resolveAuth,
189		)
190		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
191		if err != nil {
192			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
193			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
194			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
195		}
196	
197		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, a.TaskContent, deliverer)
198		if err != nil {
199			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
202		}
203		jobMetrics.RecordRun(result.Status)
204		jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
205		return finishRun(ctx, result, a.Phase)
206	}
207	
208	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
209	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
210	func finishRun(
211		ctx context.Context,
212		result *agentlib.Result,
213		phase domain.TaskPhase,
214	) error {
215		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase)
219	}
220	
221	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
222	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
223	//
224	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
225	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
226	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
227	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
228	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
229	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
230	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
231	// task).
232	//
233	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
234	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
235	func exitErrorForStatus(
236		ctx context.Context,
237		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
238		phase domain.TaskPhase,
239	) error {
240		if status == agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
241			return errors.Errorf(
242				ctx,
243				"agent reported status %q for phase %q",
244				status,
245				phase,
246			)
247		}
248		return nil
249	}
250	
251	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
252	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
253	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
254	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
255	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
256	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
257	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
258		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)
259		if claudeEnv == nil {
260			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
261		}
262		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
263			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
264		}
265		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
266			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
267		}
268		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
269			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
270		}
271		if resolvedToken != "" {
272			claudeEnv["GH_TOKEN"] = resolvedToken
273		}
274		return claudeEnv
275	}
276	
277	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
278	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
279	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
280	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
281	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
282	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
283		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
284		if err != nil {
285			return "", err
286		}
287		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
288		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
289		if resolvedToken != "" {
290			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
291				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
292			}
293		}
294		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
295			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
296		}
297		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
298		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
299		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
300		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
301		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
303		}
304		return resolvedToken, nil
305	}
306	
307	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
308	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
309	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
310	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
311	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
312	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
313	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
314	//
315	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the
316	// caller rather than stored on the argument-parsed application struct —
317	// argument/v2 panics when reflecting over unexported struct fields at startup.
318	func (a *application) resolveAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
319		hasPEMFile := a.PEMKeyFile != ""
320		hasPEMContent := a.PEMKey != ""
321		useGitHubApp := a.AppID != 0 && a.InstallationID != 0 && (hasPEMFile || hasPEMContent)
322		if useGitHubApp {
323			appCfg := githubapp.Config{AppID: a.AppID, InstallationID: a.InstallationID}
324			if hasPEMFile {
325				appCfg.PEMPath = a.PEMKeyFile
326			} else {
327				appCfg.PEM = []byte(a.PEMKey)
328			}
329			// Startup auth must not be killed by the task's work deadline: mint on a
330			// fresh bounded context (keeps ctx values, drops the caller's
331			// deadline/cancel) so a near-deadline task can't fail the token mint.
332			mintCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
333			defer cancel()
334			iat, err := githubapp.MintIAT(mintCtx, appCfg)
335			if err != nil {
336				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "mint github app iat")
337			}
338			glog.V(2).Infof(
339				"github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=github-app app_id=%d installation_id=%d",
340				a.AppID, a.InstallationID,
341			)
342			return iat, nil
343		}
344		if a.GhToken != "" {
345			glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=gh-token (raw GH_TOKEN fallback)")
346			return a.GhToken, nil
347		}
348		return "", errors.Errorf(
349			ctx,
350			"github-dark-factory-agent auth: no credentials configured — set GitHub App creds (APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, PEM_KEY_FILE or PEM_KEY) or GH_TOKEN",
351		)
352	}

1	// Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Borbe All rights reserved.

3	// license that can be found in the LICENSE file.
4	
5	package pkg
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"fmt"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"strconv"
13		"strings"
14	
15		agentlib "github.com/bborbe/agent"
16		claudelib "github.com/bborbe/agent/claude"
17		"github.com/bborbe/errors"
18		domain "github.com/bborbe/vault-cli/pkg/domain"
19		"github.com/golang/glog"
20	
21		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/git"
22		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/prompts"
23	)
24	
25	// reviewSectionHeading is the body section the ai_review phase produces. Its
26	// presence is the idempotency marker: a re-triggered ai_review phase with
27	// ## Review already written routes on the recorded verdict without re-running
28	// the (read-only but non-free) Claude review.
29	const reviewSectionHeading = "## Review"
30	
31	// ReviewOutput is the typed contract for the ## Review section. Round-trips
32	// with agentlib.MarshalSectionTyped + agentlib.ExtractSection[ReviewOutput].
33	// Outcome records the verdict (prompts.ReviewOutcomePass /
34	// prompts.ReviewOutcomeConcerns) so a replay re-routes without re-reviewing.
35	type ReviewOutput struct {
36		Repo     string `json:"repo"`
37		PRNumber int    `json:"pr_number"`
38		Outcome  string `json:"outcome"`
39		// ChecksPassed lists only the gates this run actually evaluated. An adopted
40		// result skips the worktree gates, so recording them would make the durable
41		// artifact — the human's draft→ready sign-off — attest to checks that never ran.
42		ChecksPassed []string `json:"checks_passed"`
43		// Adopted is true when the result came from an already-pushed branch head.
44		// It marks specs_completed as UNVERIFIED rather than passed: the completions
45		// live on the pushed branch, which this step deliberately does not inspect.
46		Adopted bool   `json:"adopted,omitempty"`
47		Notes   string `json:"notes"`
48	}
49	
50	// The two check sets. Keeping them named makes the skip explicit at the call
51	// site instead of hiding it in a conditional inside writeAndRoute.
52	var (
53		// checksFull are the gates a normal (lifecycle-run) result passes.
54		checksFull = []string{
55			"pr_still_draft",
56			"specs_completed",
57			"no_prompts_in_flight",
58			"diff_matches_spec_intent",
59		}
60		// checksAdopted are the gates an adopted result passes. specs_completed and
61		// no_prompts_in_flight are absent because the worktree at the task's stale
62		// `ref` cannot answer them — not because they were evaluated and passed.
63		checksAdopted = []string{
64			"pr_still_draft",
65			"diff_matches_spec_intent",
66		}
67	)
68	
69	// aiReviewStep implements agentlib.Step. It is the read-only verifier at the end
70	// of the lifecycle: it re-asserts the post-conditions deterministically (PR
71	// still draft, all matched specs completed, no prompts in-flight) then runs a
72	// read-only Claude diff-vs-spec sanity check. On a passing verdict it writes
73	// ## Review and routes to human_review (the human's draft→ready flip is the
74	// sign-off); on blocking concerns or any post-condition failure it escalates
75	// (Status: failed) per the escalation doctrine — it NEVER runs `gh pr ready`,
76	// NEVER mutates assignee/status (the controller clears assignee when
77	// phase == human_review).
78	type aiReviewStep struct {
79		github      GitHubClient
80		repoManager git.RepoManager
81		runner      claudelib.ClaudeRunner
82	}
83	
84	// NewAIReviewStep wires the ai_review step with its three IO seams: the GitHub
85	// REST client (PR draft flag), the repo manager (worktree for the spec /
86	// prompt-queue inspection), and the read-only Claude runner (diff-vs-spec
87	// sanity). The runner is injected so tests can fake the verdict without a real
88	// claude — mirroring how the execution step injects ExecutionRunner.
89	func NewAIReviewStep(
90		github GitHubClient,
91		repoManager git.RepoManager,
92		runner claudelib.ClaudeRunner,
93	) agentlib.Step {
94		return &aiReviewStep{github: github, repoManager: repoManager, runner: runner}
95	}
96	
97	// Name implements agentlib.Step.
98	func (s *aiReviewStep) Name() string { return "df-ai-review" }
99	
100	// ShouldRun always returns true. Idempotency lives INSIDE Run (## Review
101	// present → re-route on the recorded verdict) so the routing decision is never
102	// silently skipped.
103	func (s *aiReviewStep) ShouldRun(_ context.Context, _ *agentlib.Markdown) (bool, error) {
104		return true, nil
105	}
106	
107	// Run re-asserts the post-conditions, runs the read-only Claude review, writes
108	// ## Review, and routes: pass → Done + human_review; concerns → failed
109	// (escalate). Deterministic post-condition failures escalate WITHOUT writing
110	// ## Review (they are pre-checks, not a verdict).
111	func (s *aiReviewStep) Run(ctx context.Context, md *agentlib.Markdown) (*agentlib.Result, error) {
112		// Idempotency: a prior run already produced ## Review → re-route on the
113		// recorded verdict without re-reviewing.
114		if _, ok := md.FindSection(reviewSectionHeading); ok {
115			return s.routeRecorded(ctx, md)
116		}
117	
118		plan, err := agentlib.ExtractSection[PlanOutput](ctx, md, planSectionHeading)
119		if err != nil {
120			return failed("ai_review: read " + planSectionHeading + ": " + err.Error()), nil
121		}
122		// Thread the parsed result through rather than re-parsing it in review: a
123		// second extraction would have to swallow its error, and an adopted result
124		// that silently fell through to the worktree path would reproduce the very
125		// `spec … is not completed` failure the adopt path exists to avoid.
126		execOut, err := agentlib.ExtractSection[ExecutionOutput](ctx, md, resultSectionHeading)
127		if err != nil {
128			return failed("ai_review: read " + resultSectionHeading + ": " + err.Error()), nil
129		}
130	
131		fields, missing := reviewFrontmatter(md)
132		if missing != "" {
133			return needsInput("ai_review: required frontmatter field missing: " + missing), nil
134		}
135		prNumber, ok := parsePRNumber(md, fields["pr_number"])
136		if !ok {
137			return needsInput(
138				"ai_review: frontmatter pr_number is not a valid integer: " + fields["pr_number"],
139			), nil
140		}
141		owner, name, ok := parseOwnerRepo(fields["repo"])
142		if !ok {
143			return needsInput(
144				`ai_review: frontmatter "repo" must be "owner/name"; got ` + fields["repo"],
145			), nil
146		}
147	
148		return s.review(ctx, md, plan, execOut, fields, prNumber, owner, name)
149	}
150	
151	// review runs the deterministic post-condition gate, the Claude verdict, and
152	// the routing.
153	func (s *aiReviewStep) review(
154		ctx context.Context,
155		md *agentlib.Markdown,
156		plan *PlanOutput,
157		execOut *ExecutionOutput,
158		fields map[string]string,
159		prNumber int,
160		owner, name string,
161	) (*agentlib.Result, error) {
162		// (a) PR must STILL be a draft. If a human already flipped it to ready this
163		// agent must not proceed — the human took over.
164		pr, err := s.github.GetPullRequest(ctx, owner, name, prNumber)
165		if err != nil {
166			return failed(
167				fmt.Sprintf("ai_review: fetch PR %s/%s#%d: %v", owner, name, prNumber, err),
168			), nil
169		}
170		if !pr.Draft {
171			return failed(fmt.Sprintf(
172				"ai_review: PR #%d is no longer a draft (human already flipped it)", prNumber,
173			)), nil
174		}
175	
176		// An adopted result (execution found the branch already pushed and skipped
177		// the lifecycle) carries its spec completions on the REMOTE branch, not at
178		// the task's stale `ref`. Re-asserting (b) and (c) against a worktree at
179		// `ref` would therefore always fail — the original run pushed the completed
180		// specs, so the ref simply never contains them. The verdict below still
181		// runs: it reviews the PR diff, which is the adopted head.
182		if execOut.Adopted {
183			glog.V(1).Infof(
184				"ai_review: %s was adopted from pushed head %s — skipping worktree post-conditions",
185				resultSectionHeading,
186				execOut.BranchHead,
187			)
188			verdict := s.claudeVerdict(ctx, fields["repo"], prNumber, plan.MatchedSpecs)
189			return s.writeAndRoute(ctx, md, plan.Repo, prNumber, verdict, checksAdopted, true)
190		}
191	
192		worktree, err := s.repoManager.EnsureWorktree(
193			ctx, fields["clone_url"], fields["ref"], fields["task_identifier"],
194		)
195		if err != nil {
196			if git.IsGitAuthFailure(err) {
197				return needsInput(
198					"ai_review: clone failed (authentication required — set GH_TOKEN and re-trigger)",
199				), nil
200			}
201			return failed("ai_review: ensure worktree: " + err.Error()), nil
202		}
203	
204		// (b) every matched spec must now be completed.
205		specIDs := specIDsFromPaths(plan.MatchedSpecs)
206		if incomplete := firstIncompleteSpec(ctx, worktree, specIDs); incomplete != "" {
207			return failed(fmt.Sprintf(
208				"ai_review: spec %s is not completed (execution did not finish)", incomplete,
209			)), nil
210		}
211	
212		// (c) no prompts may be left in-flight.
213		if hasInProgressPrompts(worktree) {
214			return failed(
215				"ai_review: prompts still in prompts/in-progress (execution did not drain the queue)",
216			), nil
217		}
218	
219		// (d) read-only Claude diff-vs-spec sanity → verdict.
220		verdict := s.claudeVerdict(ctx, fields["repo"], prNumber, plan.MatchedSpecs)
221		return s.writeAndRoute(ctx, md, plan.Repo, prNumber, verdict, checksFull, false)
222	}
223	
224	// claudeVerdict runs the read-only review prompt and parses the structured
225	// verdict. Any runner or parse failure fails closed: it returns a concerns
226	// verdict so the human triages rather than the agent falsely passing.
227	func (s *aiReviewStep) claudeVerdict(
228		ctx context.Context,
229		repo string,
230		prNumber int,
231		matchedSpecs []string,
232	) prompts.ReviewVerdict {
233		prompt := prompts.ReviewPrompt() +
234			"\n\n## Context\n\n" +
235			"Repo: " + repo + "\n" +
236			"PR number: " + strconv.Itoa(prNumber) + "\n" +
237			"Matched specs:\n" + strings.Join(matchedSpecs, "\n") + "\n"
238	
239		result, err := s.runner.Run(ctx, prompt)
240		if err != nil {
241			glog.Warningf("ai_review: claude review call failed: %v", err)
242			return prompts.ReviewVerdict{
243				Outcome: prompts.ReviewOutcomeConcerns,
244				Notes:   "claude review unavailable: " + truncate(err.Error()),
245			}
246		}
247		verdict, err := prompts.ParseReviewVerdict(ctx, result.Result)
248		if err != nil {
249			glog.Warningf("ai_review: parse review verdict failed: %v", err)
250			return prompts.ReviewVerdict{
251				Outcome: prompts.ReviewOutcomeConcerns,
252				Notes:   "unparseable review verdict: " + truncate(err.Error()),
253			}
254		}
255		return verdict
256	}
257	
258	// writeAndRoute writes ## Review (vault-first) then routes on the verdict:
259	// pass → Done + human_review; concerns → failed (escalate). Assignee/status are
260	// never touched — the controller clears assignee when phase == human_review.
261	func (s *aiReviewStep) writeAndRoute(
262		ctx context.Context,
263		md *agentlib.Markdown,
264		repo string,
265		prNumber int,
266		verdict prompts.ReviewVerdict,
267		checks []string,
268		adopted bool,
269	) (*agentlib.Result, error) {
270		output := ReviewOutput{
271			Repo:     repo,
272			PRNumber: prNumber,
273			Outcome:  verdict.Outcome,
274			Adopted:  adopted,
275			Notes:    verdict.Notes,
276		}
277		if verdict.Outcome == prompts.ReviewOutcomePass {
278			output.ChecksPassed = checks
279		}
280		section, err := agentlib.MarshalSectionTyped(ctx, reviewSectionHeading, output)
281		if err != nil {
282			return nil, errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "marshal ## Review section")
283		}
284		md.ReplaceSection(section)
285	
286		if verdict.Outcome == prompts.ReviewOutcomePass {
287			glog.V(2).Infof("ai_review: PASS for %s#%d — routing to human_review", repo, prNumber)
288			return &agentlib.Result{
289				Status:    agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
290				NextPhase: string(domain.TaskPhaseHumanReview),
291			}, nil
292		}
293		glog.V(2).Infof("ai_review: CONCERNS for %s#%d — escalating: %s", repo, prNumber, verdict.Notes)
294		return failed("ai_review: review surfaced blocking concerns: " + verdict.Notes), nil
295	}
296	
297	// routeRecorded is the idempotency path: ## Review already exists → re-route on
298	// the recorded verdict without re-running the review. A recorded pass routes to
299	// human_review; anything else escalates.
300	func (s *aiReviewStep) routeRecorded(
301		ctx context.Context,
302		md *agentlib.Markdown,
303	) (*agentlib.Result, error) {
304		output, err := agentlib.ExtractSection[ReviewOutput](ctx, md, reviewSectionHeading)
305		if err != nil {
306			return failed("ai_review: read recorded " + reviewSectionHeading + ": " + err.Error()), nil
307		}
308		if output.Outcome == prompts.ReviewOutcomePass {
309			glog.V(2).
310				Infof("ai_review: %s already present (pass) — routing to human_review", reviewSectionHeading)
311			return &agentlib.Result{
312				Status:    agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
313				NextPhase: string(domain.TaskPhaseHumanReview),
314			}, nil
315		}
316		glog.V(2).
317			Infof("ai_review: %s already present (%s) — re-escalating", reviewSectionHeading, output.Outcome)
318		return failed("ai_review: recorded review surfaced blocking concerns: " + output.Notes), nil
319	}

321	// reviewFrontmatter reads the frontmatter fields the ai_review step needs.
322	// Returns the first missing field's name ("" if all present) and the values.
323	func reviewFrontmatter(md *agentlib.Markdown) (map[string]string, string) {
324		keys := []string{"repo", "pr_number", "clone_url", "ref", "task_identifier"}
325		values := map[string]string{}
326		for _, key := range keys {
327			v, _ := md.Frontmatter.String(key)
328			if strings.TrimSpace(v) == "" {
329				// pr_number may be a YAML int — recover it before declaring missing.
330				if key == "pr_number" {
331					if n, ok := md.Frontmatter.Int(key); ok {
332						values[key] = strconv.Itoa(n)
333						continue
334					}
335				}
336				return values, key
337			}
338			values[key] = v
339		}
340		return values, ""
341	}

343	// firstIncompleteSpec returns the id of the first spec that is NOT completed, or
344	// "" when every spec is completed. A spec is completed when it has moved to
345	// specs/completed/<id>.md OR its specs/in-progress/<id>.md carries frontmatter
346	// completed:true (reusing the frontmatterTruthy contract from planning).
347	func firstIncompleteSpec(ctx context.Context, worktree string, specIDs []string) string {
348		for _, id := range specIDs {
349			if !specCompleted(ctx, worktree, id) {
350				return id
351			}
352		}
353		return ""
354	}
355	
356	// specCompleted reports whether spec <id> reached the completed terminal state.
357	func specCompleted(ctx context.Context, worktree, id string) bool {
358		if fileExists(filepath.Join(worktree, "specs", "completed", id+".md")) {
359			return true
360		}
361		path := filepath.Join(worktree, "specs", "in-progress", id+".md")
362		content, err := os.ReadFile(path) // #nosec G304 -- path from validated worktree + spec id
363		if err != nil {
364			return false
365		}
366		parsed, err := agentlib.ParseMarkdown(ctx, string(content))
367		if err != nil {
368			return false
369		}
370		return frontmatterTruthy(parsed.Frontmatter, "completed")
371	}

20	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
21	// the executor that watches its Job.
22	//
23	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
24	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
25	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
26	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
27	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
28	//
29	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
30	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
31	// parked at human_review.
32	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
33		ctx := context.Background()
34		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
35	
36		cases := []struct {
37			name    string
38			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
39			wantErr bool
40		}{
41			{
42				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
43				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
44				wantErr: true,
45			},
46			{
47				name:    "done exits 0",
48				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
49				wantErr: false,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
58				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
59				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
60				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
61				wantErr: false,
62			},
63		}
64	
65		for _, c := range cases {
66			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
67				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase)
68				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
69					t.Fatalf(
70						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
71						c.status,
72					)
73				}
74				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
75					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
76				}
77			})
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken guards the startup argument dump against
82	// republishing the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN value into the Job log.
83	//
84	// argument.Print honours only display:"hidden" and display:"length"; every other
85	// tag value falls through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`). The root
86	// binary's application struct carried display:"password" — a value the printer does
87	// not implement — so each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in
88	// cleartext. This test drives the real printer over the real struct, so removing
89	// the display:"length" tag turns it red.
90	//
91	// Plain testing rather than Ginkgo on purpose: application is unexported, so the
92	// assertion must live in package main, and package main_test (main_test.go) shares
93	// this test binary — where a second RunSpecs fails with "calling RunSpecs more than
94	// once". An internal spec therefore cannot join the existing suite. Same shape as
95	// TestExitErrorForStatus above.
96	func TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
97		const sentinel = "sentinel-token-do-not-log-9f3a2b7c1d"
98	
99		var buf bytes.Buffer
100		log.SetOutput(&buf)
101		log.SetFlags(0)
102		defer func() {
103			log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
104			log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
105		}()
106	
107		if err := argument.Print(context.Background(), &application{AnthropicAuthToken: sentinel}); err != nil {
108			t.Fatalf("print: %v", err)
109		}
110	
111		rendered := buf.String()
112		if got := strings.Count(rendered, sentinel); got != 0 {
113			t.Fatalf(
114				"token value leaked into the argument dump: sentinel appeared %d times\n%s",
115				got,
116				rendered,
117			)
118		}
119		if got := strings.Count(rendered, "AnthropicAuthToken"); got != 1 {
120			t.Fatalf("want the field named exactly once, got %d\n%s", got, rendered)
121		}
122		if !strings.Contains(rendered, "Argument: AnthropicAuthToken length ") {
123			t.Fatalf("want the length form, got:\n%s", rendered)
124		}
125	}

14	// — no GitHub App required. Point it at a real draft PR (planning phase needs
15	// the GitHub REST API) or a local sandbox repo.

78	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
79		taskContent, err := os.ReadFile(
80			a.TaskFilePath,
81		) // #nosec G304 -- filePath from trusted CLI input
82		if err != nil {
83			return errors.Wrapf(ctx, err, "read task file: %s", a.TaskFilePath)
84		}
85	
86		reposPath, workPath, err := a.resolveCachePaths(ctx)
87		if err != nil {
88			return err
89		}
90		ghToken := a.resolveGhToken(ctx)
91	
92		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs("")
93		if claudeEnv == nil {
94			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
95		}
96		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
97			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
98		}
99		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
100			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
101		}
102		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
103			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
104		}
105	
106		deliverer := factory.CreateFileResultDeliverer(a.TaskFilePath)
107		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(reposPath, workPath, ghToken)
108		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(ghToken)
109		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
110	
111		agent := factory.CreateAgent(
112			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
113			a.AgentDir,
114			a.AnthropicModel,
115			ghToken,
116			claudeEnv,
117			repoManager,
118			githubClient,
119			claudeProber,
120			// Local CLI path: the credential is the operator's own long-lived gh
121			// token, so there is nothing to refresh before the push.
122			nil,
123		)
124	
125		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, string(taskContent), deliverer)
126		if err != nil {
127			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
128		}
129		return agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result)
130	}

132	// resolveCachePaths fills in defaults for ReposPath/WorkPath when unset
133	// (~/.cache/github-dark-factory-agent/{repos,work}). The pod entry point
134	// requires explicit /repos and /work mounts; local CLI usage benefits from a
135	// default.
136	func (a *application) resolveCachePaths(ctx context.Context) (string, string, error) {
137		reposPath := a.ReposPath
138		workPath := a.WorkPath
139		if reposPath != "" && workPath != "" {
140			return reposPath, workPath, nil
141		}
142		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
143		if err != nil {
144			return "", "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "resolve user home dir")
145		}
146		if reposPath == "" {
147			reposPath = filepath.Join(home, ".cache", "github-dark-factory-agent", "repos")
148		}
149		if workPath == "" {
150			workPath = filepath.Join(home, ".cache", "github-dark-factory-agent", "work")
151		}
152		return reposPath, workPath, nil
153	}

156	// token` for ambient local auth. An empty result is returned when neither is
157	// available (the gh-token preflight then escalates cleanly).
158	func (a *application) resolveGhToken(ctx context.Context) string {
159		if a.GhToken != "" {
160			return a.GhToken
161		}
162		// #nosec G204 -- fixed argv; no user-controlled input reaches the command line
163		out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "gh", "auth", "token").Output()
164		if err != nil {
165			glog.V(2).
166				Infof("run-task: `gh auth token` unavailable (%v) — proceeding without a token", err)
167			return ""
168		}
169		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
170	}

# Sentry

[![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/bborbe/sentry.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/bborbe/sentry)
[![CI](https://github.com/bborbe/sentry/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bborbe/sentry/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/bborbe/sentry)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/bborbe/sentry)

A Go library that provides an enhanced wrapper around the [Sentry Go SDK](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-go) with additional functionality for error exclusion, automatic tag enrichment, and context data extraction.

## Features

- **Automatic Tag Enrichment**: Extracts data from context and errors to add as Sentry tags
- **Error Filtering**: Configurable error exclusion to prevent noise
- **Context Integration**: Uses `github.com/bborbe/errors` for context data extraction
- **Proxy Support**: HTTP transport wrapper for proxy configurations
- **Type-Safe Interface**: Clean interface abstraction with mock generation support

## Installation

```bash
go get github.com/bborbe/sentry
```

## Quick Start

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "time"

    "github.com/bborbe/errors"
    "github.com/bborbe/sentry"
    "github.com/getsentry/sentry-go"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Create client with options
    client, err := sentry.NewClient(ctx, sentry.ClientOptions{
        Dsn: "your-sentry-dsn-here",
        Tags: map[string]string{
            "service": "my-app",
            "version": "1.0.0",
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    defer func() {
        client.Flush(2 * time.Second)
        client.Close()
    }()

    // Add context data
    ctx = errors.AddToContext(ctx, "user_id", "12345")
    
    // Create error with data
    err = errors.AddDataToError(
        errors.New("something went wrong"),
        map[string]string{"operation": "user_login"},
    )

    // Capture exception with automatic tag enrichment
    client.CaptureException(err, &sentry.EventHint{
        Context: ctx,
        Data: map[string]interface{}{
            "request_id": "req-abc123",
            "retries": 3,
        },
    }, sentry.NewScope())
}
```

## Core Components

### Client Interface

The main interface provides these methods:

```go
type Client interface {
    CaptureMessage(message string, hint *sentry.EventHint, scope sentry.EventModifier) *sentry.EventID
    CaptureException(exception error, hint *sentry.EventHint, scope sentry.EventModifier) *sentry.EventID
    Flush(timeout time.Duration) bool
    io.Closer
}
```

### Error Exclusion

Filter out specific errors to reduce noise:

```go
excludeFunc := func(err error) bool {
    return errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)
}

client, err := sentry.NewClient(ctx, clientOptions, excludeFunc)
```

### Automatic Tag Enrichment

The client automatically extracts and adds tags from:
- Context data (using `github.com/bborbe/errors`)
- Error data (attached to errors)
- Hint data (passed in EventHint)

## API Documentation

For detailed API documentation, visit [pkg.go.dev/github.com/bborbe/sentry](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/bborbe/sentry).

## Dependencies

This library integrates closely with:
- **github.com/bborbe/errors**: Enhanced context and error data extraction
- **github.com/getsentry/sentry-go**: Official Sentry Go SDK (v0.36.0+)

The integration with `bborbe/errors` enables automatic extraction of context data and error metadata as Sentry tags.

## Development

### Running Tests
```bash
make test
```

### Code Generation (Mocks)
```bash
make generate
```

### Full Pre-commit Workflow
```bash
make precommit  # Format, generate, test, and lint
```

# Definition of Done

The validation prompt dark-factory runs against each executed prompt before it
marks the prompt complete. A change is Done only when every box holds.

- [ ] Builds: `make precommit` exits 0 (generate + format + test + lint + vet + gosec + coverage).
- [ ] Tests: new/changed behavior has Ginkgo coverage; boundaries are mocked (counterfeiter), the framework Agent is not.
- [ ] Scope: the diff touches only what the spec asked for; no unrelated files.
- [ ] Errors: wrapped via `github.com/bborbe/errors`; no bare `return err`, no `fmt.Errorf`.
- [ ] Escalation doctrine: failure paths return `Status: failed`/`needs_input` without mutating `assignee`/`status` or writing a `## Failure` section.
- [ ] Docs: user-facing behavior changes are reflected in `docs/` and the CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` section.

# Prompt Writing Guide

A prompt is a markdown file that tells the YOLO agent what to build. Each prompt produces one atomic, verifiable change.

## When to Write a Prompt

**This document does NOT decide direct vs prompt vs spec.** That decision lives in [../choosing-a-flow.md](../choosing-a-flow.md) — the single source of truth. Read it first to confirm a prompt is the right flow.

In short: write a prompt when the change is a code change that does NOT carry a business-level "why" that deserves its own document. Markdown / docs / configs / small operator scripts → direct edits, not prompts. Features with a real business-why → spec first. See the canonical decision doc.

You may also write prompts manually for finer control over decomposition from an approved spec (the daemon does this automatically by default).

## Creating a Prompt

Use the Claude Code command:

```
/dark-factory:create-prompt
```

Or create manually. Location depends on status and project config:

| Status | Directory | Purpose |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `idea` | `prompts/ideas/` | Rough concepts, not ready for approval |
| `draft` | inbox dir (default: `prompts/`) | Complete prompts, ready for review and approval |

The inbox directory is configurable per project. Run `dark-factory config` to check the actual `inboxDir` path before writing prompts.

```bash
# Check your project's inbox directory
dark-factory config | grep inboxDir

# Idea — park it for later
touch prompts/ideas/my-change.md

# Draft — ready for review (use the inboxDir from config)
touch prompts/my-change.md
```

Use lowercase-kebab-case. Dark-factory assigns execution numbers on approve (e.g., `248-spec-044-model.md`).

**Ordering prefix for dependent prompts.** When multiple prompts must execute in strict order, prefix with a simple number to define the sequence: `1-spec-044-model.md`, `2-spec-044-executor-timeout.md`, `3-spec-044-processor-retry.md`. Approve them in order — dark-factory replaces the prefix with execution numbers. Do NOT number standalone prompts.

## Prompt Structure

### Frontmatter

```yaml
---
status: draft
---
```

Required for every prompt derived from a spec — the field is not optional there:

```yaml
---
spec: ["030-foo-bar-baz"]
status: draft
created: "2026-03-11T10:00:00Z"
---
```

A spec is linked to its prompts **only** through this field: dark-factory advances the spec to `verifying` when the prompts carrying that link are complete, so a prompt without it leaves the spec stuck at `prompted` forever. Omit `spec` only for a prompt that has no spec at all.

- `spec` must be a YAML array of strings — single or multiple entries
- **Canonical form is the full slug** (e.g. `["030-foo-bar-baz"]`), not the bare number. Daemon-generated prompts use this form, and `pkg/slugmigrator` rewrites bare numbers to full slugs after each generation cycle so all prompts converge on the canonical form
- Bare numbers (`spec: ["030"]`) are accepted as input — the slug migrator resolves them to the full form at the next daemon iteration
- Only use `spec`, `status`, `created`, `issue` — dark-factory adds the rest
- Valid inbox statuses: `idea` (rough concept, needs refinement) or `draft` (complete, ready for approval)

### Body

```xml
<summary>
5-10 bullet points describing WHAT this prompt achieves, not HOW.
Written for human review — no file paths, no struct names.

GOOD:

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## v0.6.2

- fix: link the pinned dark-factory clone to `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/dark-factory` so the authoring-rule paths the agents hardcode resolve — a local-path `marketplace add` never creates that directory, so prompt generation ran with no guides

## v0.6.1

- chore: restate the `do-not-merge` gate message to name its bypass actors — the Admin repository role and Integration `3907226`, both `bypass_mode: always` in the `master-protection` ruleset — instead of asserting an unqualified block

## v0.6.0

- feat: **build the release image on a cluster (`BUILD_TARGET=sun`), not only locally.** `make build` had a single arm — a local `docker build` — so publishing a release required a Docker daemon and `docker push` on the workstation. An agent is refused `docker push`, which made a release image unpublishable without a human at the keyboard. `Makefile.docker` now carries two arms, ported from `bborbe/a2a-worker-controller` and `bborbe/agent-claude`: `BUILD_TARGET=local` (the default, unchanged behaviour) and any other value, which renders `hack/build-job.yaml` as a Job on that cluster and pushes from inside it. The vendored `hack/` set is `a2a-worker-controller`'s hardened copy — templated namespace, `case`-based value whitelisting, no service-account token — rather than `agent-claude`'s older one. The cluster arm refuses to run without an explicit `VERSION` (the Makefile default is the newest release tag, so a defaulted build would overwrite a published image with one built from a different commit) and refuses to push a `vX.Y.Z` tag from any `REF` other than that tag. `upload` and `clean` are guarded so a remote build does not fail at a push step for an image that was never local. `Dockerfile` gains a `go mod vendor` step in its build stage: the local arm got `vendor/` from `check-go-mod`, but the cluster arm clones a git ref where `vendor/` is gitignored, so `-mod=vendor` would have failed there. `make precommit` now runs `shellcheck -S warning` over `hack/*.sh`, since those scripts handle the teamvault→Secret credential path

## v0.5.14

- fix: **redact the `AnthropicAuthToken` value from the startup argument dump.** The root binary's `application` struct carried `display:"password"` — a tag the argument printer does not implement. It honours only `display:"hidden"` and `display:"length"`, so every other value fell through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`) and each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in cleartext into the cluster Job log. The field now carries `display:"length"`, matching the sibling in `cmd/run-task`, so the dump names the key and its length and never the value. A regression spec drives the real printer over the real struct and fails if the redaction is removed

## v0.5.13

- test: **cover the per-prompt setup fetch, not only the push.** `v0.5.12` moved the credential to a file-backed git helper, but only the push site had a regression spec — the fetch site (the one that failed first on 2026-11-03) was pinned by nothing. The new spec starts with token `A`, lets the lifecycle refresher mint `B`, and asserts the credential `git credential fill` resolves *during* the run is `B` — the A→B shape a "file is non-empty" check would not discriminate. No production code changes

## v0.5.12

- fix: **install a file-backed git credential helper so a long lifecycle run never uses an expired token.** The GitHub App installation token lives 60 minutes and is minted once at startup; `gh auth setup-git` binds it into a helper that resolves `GH_TOKEN` from the environment of whatever runs git, and the dark-factory daemon captured that environment when it was started — so no refresh in the parent process can reach it. A token file has no such lifetime: git re-reads it at every credential lookup. Observed 2026-11-03 on `bborbe/trading#433`: token minted 18:10Z, the daemon's own `git fetch origin` refused at 19:15Z with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported`

## v0.5.11

- fix: **exit non-zero when the agent publishes `Status: failed`.** The result was still published to the task, but the process returned nil, so the Job completed and the executor — which records a phase success on exit 0 alone (`IsJobSucceeded` in `agent-task-executor`'s `job_watcher`) and never reads the published Status — wrote a *phase success* for a run that had failed. Once the success grace expired the task was parked at `human_review` as though a human had parked it deliberately. Observed 2026-11-03 on task `ceb79961`: a Job that published `Status: failed` for `git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443` exited 0 and parked the task. `needs_input` is deliberately unchanged — parking for a human answer is that status's intent

## v0.5.10

- chore: update github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.138.0, github.com/bborbe/cqrs to v0.6.15, github.com/bborbe/errors to v1.6.6, github.com/bborbe/kafka to v1.29.11, github.com/bborbe/maintainer to v0.51.0, github.com/bborbe/sentry to v1.10.7, github.com/bborbe/service to v1.11.2, github.com/bborbe/time to v1.27.25, github.com/bborbe/vault-cli to v0.186.2, github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 to v2.34.0

//
// AddGlobalEventProcessor is deprecated. Most users will prefer to initialize
// the SDK with Init and provide a ClientOptions.BeforeSend function or use
// Scope.AddEventProcessor instead.
func AddGlobalEventProcessor(processor EventProcessor) {

	Name() string

<summary>
- A failed agent phase now reports the phase's own message in the error, so the Sentry issue says why the phase failed instead of only that the status was "failed".
- Sentry groups failures separately for planning, execution, and ai_review, so one phase's failures no longer disappear into another phase's issue.
- Each failure event carries the phase and status as Sentry tags, making the event self-describing when it arrives.
- Escalation is unchanged: a failed result still makes the Job exit non-zero.
- Events from unrelated errors are not re-grouped; only errors that carry a phase are fingerprinted.
- The fix works through the existing `service.Main` capture path without double-reporting the same failure.
- Tests cover the message in the error, the phase/status data on the error, the fingerprint processor, and a real capture through the Sentry client.
- A changelog entry records the operator-visible change.
- ai_review fail-closed routing is deliberately untouched in this change.
</summary>

<objective>
Make a failed phase's Sentry event self-describing and separable: include `Result.Message` in the error raised by `exitErrorForStatus`, attach the phase and status to the error so they become Sentry tags, and assign a per-phase Sentry fingerprint so planning/execution/ai_review failures no longer collapse into one untriageable issue. The Job must still exit non-zero on failure.
</objective>

<context>

Project:
- `main.go` — the Kafka entry point. Read `main`, `application.Run`, `finishRun`, and `exitErrorForStatus`. This is the only place the bug lives.
- `main_internal_test.go` — the existing `TestExitErrorForStatus` guards the exit-code contract; it is plain `testing` in `package main` on purpose (the external `main_test` package already calls `RunSpecs`, so a second suite would fail).

   ```go
   func exitErrorForStatus(
       ctx context.Context,
       status agentlib.AgentStatus,
       phase domain.TaskPhase,
       message string,
   ) error {
       if status != agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
           return nil
       }
       msg := strings.TrimSpace(message)
       var err error
       if msg == "" {
           err = errors.Errorf(ctx, "agent reported status %q for phase %q", status, phase)
       } else {
           err = errors.Errorf(
               ctx,
               "agent reported status %q for phase %q: %s",
               status,
               phase,
               msg,
           )
       }
       return errors.AddDataToError(err, map[string]any{
           "phase":  string(phase),
           "status": string(status),
       })
   }
   ```

   `errors` is `github.com/bborbe/errors`; `AddDataToError` returns a `DataError` whose `Data()` is read by `libsentry`'s `enrichEventTags` and by the fingerprint processor below. Add `"strings"` to the imports.

2. Update the caller in `finishRun` to pass the message:

   ```go
   return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase, result.Message)
   ```

   Do not change `finishRun`'s signature or the fact that its error is returned from `application.Run` unchanged (do not wrap it before returning, or the Sentry event hint will see a wrapper instead of the `DataError`).

   ```go
   // phaseFingerprintProcessor is a global Sentry event processor that assigns
   // a per-phase fingerprint to the event captured from a failed phase.
   //
   // service.Main captures the error Run returns with a fresh
   // sentry.NewScope(), so the application cannot attach a fingerprint to that
   // capture through the scope. A global event processor is the only hook that
   // runs after that scope is applied and before the event is sent. It leaves
   // every event without phase data untouched, so it cannot re-group unrelated
   // captures.
   func phaseFingerprintProcessor(
       event *sentrygo.Event,
       hint *sentrygo.EventHint,
   ) *sentrygo.Event {
       if event == nil || hint == nil || hint.OriginalException == nil {
           return event
       }
       phase, ok := errors.DataFromError(hint.OriginalException)["phase"].(string)
       if !ok || phase == "" {
           return event
       }
       event.Fingerprint = []string{"github-dark-factory-agent", "phase", phase}
       return event
   }
   ```

   In `main()`:

   ```go
   func main() {
       sentrygo.AddGlobalEventProcessor(phaseFingerprintProcessor)
       app := &application{}
       os.Exit(service.Main(context.Background(), app, &app.SentryDSN, &app.SentryProxy))
   }
   ```

   - Call `exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase, c.message)`.

   - For every non-failed case, assert `err == nil` as before.

       event := phaseFingerprintProcessor(
           &sentrygo.Event{},
           &sentrygo.EventHint{OriginalException: errors.New(context.Background(), "unrelated")},

       if len(event.Fingerprint) != 0 {

       }
   }
   ```

Register the processor, build a real `libsentry.NewClient` with a recording transport, capture the error produced by `exitErrorForStatus`, and assert the recorded event. Use these exact types (verify the `sentrygo.Transport` interface in the module cache if it has changed):

   ```go
   type recordingTransport struct {
       events []*sentrygo.Event
   }

   func (t *recordingTransport) Configure(_ sentrygo.ClientOptions) {}
   func (t *recordingTransport) SendEvent(event *sentrygo.Event) {
       t.events = append(t.events, event)
   }
   func (t *recordingTransport) Flush(_ time.Duration) bool { return true }
   func (t *recordingTransport) FlushWithContext(_ context.Context) bool { return true }
   func (t *recordingTransport) Close() {}
   ```

   ```go

       ctx := context.Background()
       sentrygo.AddGlobalEventProcessor(phaseFingerprintProcessor)

       transport := &recordingTransport{}
       client, err := libsentry.NewClient(ctx, sentrygo.ClientOptions{

       })

           event.Fingerprint[1] != "phase" ||
           event.Fingerprint[2] != "ai_review" {

       }
       if event.Tags["phase"] != "ai_review" {
           t.Fatalf("want phase tag ai_review, got %q", event.Tags["phase"])
       }
       if event.Tags["status"] != "failed" {
           t.Fatalf("want status tag failed, got %q", event.Tags["status"])
       }
   }

120	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
121		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
122		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())
123		pusher := push.New(a.PushgatewayURL, libmetrics.BuildJobMetricsName(agentName)).
124			Grouping("agent", agentName).
125			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
126			Collector(registry)
127		defer func() {
128			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
129				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)
130				return
131			}
132			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
133		}()
134		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
135	
136		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
137	
138		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
139		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
140		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
141		if err != nil {
142			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
143			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
144			return err
145		}
146	
147		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
148		if a.TaskID != "" {
149			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
150				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
151				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
152				return errors.Errorf(ctx, "KAFKA_BROKERS must be set when TASK_ID is set")
153			}
154			syncProducer, err := factory.CreateSyncProducer(ctx, a.KafkaBrokers)
155			if err != nil {
156				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
157				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
158				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
159			}
160			defer func() {
161				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
162					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
163				}
164			}()
165			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
166				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
167				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
168			)
169		}
170	
171		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
172	
173		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
174		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
175		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
176		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
177			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
178			a.AgentDir,
179			a.AnthropicModel,
180			resolvedToken,
181			claudeEnv,
182			repoManager,
183			githubClient,
184			claudeProber,
185			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
186			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
187			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
188			a.resolveAuth,
189		)
190		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
191		if err != nil {
192			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
193			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
194			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
195		}
196	
197		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, a.TaskContent, deliverer)
198		if err != nil {
199			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
202		}
203		jobMetrics.RecordRun(result.Status)
204		jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
205		return finishRun(ctx, result, a.Phase)
206	}
207	
208	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
209	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
210	func finishRun(
211		ctx context.Context,
212		result *agentlib.Result,
213		phase domain.TaskPhase,
214	) error {
215		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase)
219	}
220	
221	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
222	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
223	//
224	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
225	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
226	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
227	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
228	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
229	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
230	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
231	// task).
232	//
233	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
234	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
235	func exitErrorForStatus(
236		ctx context.Context,
237		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
238		phase domain.TaskPhase,
239	) error {
240		if status == agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
241			return errors.Errorf(
242				ctx,
243				"agent reported status %q for phase %q",
244				status,
245				phase,
246			)
247		}
248		return nil
249	}
250	
251	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
252	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
253	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
254	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
255	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
256	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
257	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
258		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)
259		if claudeEnv == nil {
260			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
261		}
262		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
263			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
264		}
265		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
266			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
267		}
268		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
269			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
270		}
271		if resolvedToken != "" {
272			claudeEnv["GH_TOKEN"] = resolvedToken
273		}
274		return claudeEnv
275	}
276	
277	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
278	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
279	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
280	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
281	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
282	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
283		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
284		if err != nil {
285			return "", err
286		}
287		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
288		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
289		if resolvedToken != "" {
290			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
291				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
292			}
293		}
294		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
295			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
296		}
297		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
298		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
299		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
300		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
301		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
303		}
304		return resolvedToken, nil
305	}
306	
307	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
308	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
309	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
310	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
311	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
312	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
313	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
314	//
315	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the
316	// caller rather than stored on the argument-parsed application struct —
317	// argument/v2 panics when reflecting over unexported struct fields at startup.
318	func (a *application) resolveAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
319		hasPEMFile := a.PEMKeyFile != ""
320		hasPEMContent := a.PEMKey != ""
321		useGitHubApp := a.AppID != 0 && a.InstallationID != 0 && (hasPEMFile || hasPEMContent)
322		if useGitHubApp {
323			appCfg := githubapp.Config{AppID: a.AppID, InstallationID: a.InstallationID}
324			if hasPEMFile {
325				appCfg.PEMPath = a.PEMKeyFile
326			} else {
327				appCfg.PEM = []byte(a.PEMKey)
328			}
329			// Startup auth must not be killed by the task's work deadline: mint on a
330			// fresh bounded context (keeps ctx values, drops the caller's
331			// deadline/cancel) so a near-deadline task can't fail the token mint.
332			mintCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
333			defer cancel()
334			iat, err := githubapp.MintIAT(mintCtx, appCfg)
335			if err != nil {
336				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "mint github app iat")
337			}
338			glog.V(2).Infof(
339				"github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=github-app app_id=%d installation_id=%d",
340				a.AppID, a.InstallationID,
341			)
342			return iat, nil
343		}
344		if a.GhToken != "" {
345			glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=gh-token (raw GH_TOKEN fallback)")
346			return a.GhToken, nil
347		}
348		return "", errors.Errorf(
349			ctx,
350			"github-dark-factory-agent auth: no credentials configured — set GitHub App creds (APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, PEM_KEY_FILE or PEM_KEY) or GH_TOKEN",
351		)
352	}

20	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
21	// the executor that watches its Job.
22	//
23	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
24	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
25	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
26	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
27	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
28	//
29	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
30	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
31	// parked at human_review.
32	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
33		ctx := context.Background()
34		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
35	
36		cases := []struct {
37			name    string
38			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
39			wantErr bool
40		}{
41			{
42				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
43				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
44				wantErr: true,
45			},
46			{
47				name:    "done exits 0",
48				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
49				wantErr: false,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
58				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
59				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
60				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
61				wantErr: false,
62			},
63		}
64	
65		for _, c := range cases {
66			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
67				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase)
68				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
69					t.Fatalf(
70						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
71						c.status,
72					)
73				}
74				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
75					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
76				}
77			})
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken guards the startup argument dump against
82	// republishing the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN value into the Job log.
83	//
84	// argument.Print honours only display:"hidden" and display:"length"; every other
85	// tag value falls through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`). The root
86	// binary's application struct carried display:"password" — a value the printer does
87	// not implement — so each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in
88	// cleartext. This test drives the real printer over the real struct, so removing
89	// the display:"length" tag turns it red.
90	//
91	// Plain testing rather than Ginkgo on purpose: application is unexported, so the
92	// assertion must live in package main, and package main_test (main_test.go) shares
93	// this test binary — where a second RunSpecs fails with "calling RunSpecs more than
94	// once". An internal spec therefore cannot join the existing suite. Same shape as
95	// TestExitErrorForStatus above.
96	func TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
97		const sentinel = "sentinel-token-do-not-log-9f3a2b7c1d"
98	
99		var buf bytes.Buffer
100		log.SetOutput(&buf)
101		log.SetFlags(0)
102		defer func() {
103			log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
104			log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
105		}()
106	
107		if err := argument.Print(context.Background(), &application{AnthropicAuthToken: sentinel}); err != nil {
108			t.Fatalf("print: %v", err)
109		}
110	
111		rendered := buf.String()
112		if got := strings.Count(rendered, sentinel); got != 0 {
113			t.Fatalf(
114				"token value leaked into the argument dump: sentinel appeared %d times\n%s",
115				got,
116				rendered,
117			)
118		}
119		if got := strings.Count(rendered, "AnthropicAuthToken"); got != 1 {
120			t.Fatalf("want the field named exactly once, got %d\n%s", got, rendered)
121		}
122		if !strings.Contains(rendered, "Argument: AnthropicAuthToken length ") {
123			t.Fatalf("want the length form, got:\n%s", rendered)
124		}
125	}
